public_comment.topic: Asked for a multi-year budget projection rather than one year, how many new personnel the budgets represent, and the anticipated salary for a proposed town manager assistant; noted a $3 million override figure already being discussed.
Said the May Institute grant is money well spent, and argued the town should raise the levy limit now to invest and earn interest income rather than pursue an operating override.

votes.outcome: passed (roll call: Tom I, Mike I, Anna I, Tanya I, Jay I, chair I)

budget_items.what_was_said: The IT department requested an FY27 budget reflecting roughly a 9% increase over the prior year, driven by loss of one-time ARPA funding for MUNIS, corrected telephone budgeting, and rising contracted services costs.
MUNIS was partly paid through ARPA in FY26 and now must be budgeted at full cost.
Reducing on-site IT support from 4 to a possible 3 days a week in FY27 would offset costs.
Not renewing Clear Gov software produces a savings that partially offsets other IT cost increases.

budget_items.topic: Adult Activity Center IT capital request
budget_items.what_was_said: A capital request for access points and server upgrades at the senior/adult activity center did not make the initial cutline but may be funded via a community compact IT grant.
The town breaks down its Microsoft licensing by tier: standard, basic, exchange, and premium, covering both employees and boards/committees.
A committee member questioned the cost of the Code Red emergency notification subscription relative to how many residents actually subscribe.
A portion of OpenGov's cost is offset by technology fees paid by users of online permitting, funneled through the tech revolving fund.

The superintendent gave the FY26 baseline: salaries, expenses, and a total that included a one-time free cash allocation used to offset health insurance, unemployment insurance, salaries, and athletic transportation.
School choice revenue received by the district has fallen sharply over the years, shifting that burden to the local taxpayer.
Extended day, lunch, and sped tuition circuit breaker were called out as the largest revolving revenue generators; the school choice "other" line includes bus fees collected early.
A member argued athletic fees should be required to cover athletic transportation costs, noting that doing so would wipe out the athletic revolving account.
Title I funding is expected to change significantly for FY27 versus FY26, with the district unsure of the exact allocation.
Title II, the main professional development funding vehicle, is projected lower for FY27.
Title IV funding, for safe and supportive school environments, is anticipated to be very small for FY27.
The special education entitlement grant largely funds one very expensive out-of-district placement at the May Institute/May Center.
Circuit breaker reimbursement is generally around a set percentage of the prior year's out-of-district tuition, rarely fully funded.
This is the second and final year of a two-year Student Opportunity Act grant, previously used to fund a literacy coach and now redirected to early literacy materials and professional development.
The state delegation secured earmarks for one-time costs; the FY27 amount is unknown, with prior earmarks discussed for use toward unfunded capital projects.
Health insurance is budgeted at current staff plans plus a percentage increase, plus new restored positions budgeted at the highest family plan tier as a conservative assumption.

The business manager budgeted a percentage increase for busing pending confirmation from the bus contractor, citing a memo with the actual contracted rate; the district has had four consecutive multi-year contracts with only one bidder.
Extra buses beyond the contracted set carry a per-bus, per-day surcharge on top of the base rate.

budget_items.topic: Total estimated cost of restored positions/restructuring
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent totaled the cost of all proposed restored positions and central office restructuring, assuming highest-tier health insurance for all new hires.
The business manager stated the full FY27 salary and expense totals that make up the override-level budget ask.

budget_items.topic: Budget line savings found before submission
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent and business manager found additional savings by revisiting the posted budget, partly by converting a proposed full-time athletic director into a half-time position.
Restoring the bridge program requires a teacher and a paraprofessional; costs were given separately for salary and insurance.

Proposed changes include eliminating a grant-funded literacy coach, moving a math coach to an instructional-specialist/teacher salary line, and adding a 0.5 data reporting manager and a 1.0 assistant business manager position.
A committee member questioned the cost of maintaining a full-time athletic trainer alongside a part-time athletic director as an outlier compared to peer districts.
A proposal to contract out social-emotional services (e.g., via Seven Hills or Community Health Link) was debated against keeping in-house school social workers given crisis response needs.

budget_items.topic: Proposed alternative to override: raise levy limit to invest
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident proposed increasing the levy limit to generate investment interest income as an alternative/supplement to an operating override, citing an estimated override figure and per-thousand tax impact.

transfers.description: Salary reserve line transfer to departments to account for a mid-year reclassification/regrade (e.g., the communications/IT manager position) approved at town meeting.
Routine line-item transfers between school budget lines as needs change during the year, each individually voted by the school committee.

decisions.decision: The business manager will compile forward-looking EPIMS staffing trend data for the Finance Committee and the tri-board going forward.
IT will look into and report back the number of Code Red subscribers.
The business manager will find out how much the school solar installations (high school and Turkey Hill) offset the electric bill.
Souza IT will provide a breakdown of Microsoft license cost by employees vs. boards/committees.
The schools will receive a single allocated line within the town's balanced budget constrained by Prop 2½; if an override fails, the district must reduce its ask down to that balanced number.
Finance Committee liaison/board assignments will be revisited later, likely after town meeting.
The March 12 Finance Committee meeting will review smaller department budgets including Council on Aging and Board of Health; the chair will be absent and another member will chair.
The tri-board will meet March 11 to discuss override structure (single-year vs. multi-year, use of excess levy capacity) before it goes to the Select Board for the warrant.

minutes.headline: School Committee says only a townwide override can restore positions cut last year, not a smaller fix.
minutes.summary: The Finance Committee heard the IT department's FY27 budget request and a detailed FY27 school budget presentation focused on restoring special education, literacy, and student-services positions cut the prior year. No formal budget votes were taken; the meeting was discussion and Q&A ahead of a March 11 tri-board meeting where override strategy will be decided, with the School Committee chair stating a townwide operating override is necessary to avoid what he called "catastrophic" cuts.

what_happened.line: The School Committee chair said a townwide operating override, not a smaller fix, is needed to avoid what he called "catastrophic" cuts.
The district's FY27 school budget presentation focused on restoring special education, literacy, and student-services positions cut the prior year.
No budget votes were taken; the schools will get a single line within the town's balanced budget, and the district must scale its ask down to that number if an override fails.
IT presented an FY27 request driven largely by the loss of one-time ARPA funding that had covered MUNIS software.
The business manager agreed to compile ongoing EPIMS staffing trend data for the Finance Committee and the tri-board.

why_it_matters: An operating override, if pursued, would go to voters and change property tax bills beyond the normal 2½ percent cap.
The positions under discussion -- special education, literacy, and student-services roles cut last year -- affect direct school services to students.
Override structure and size will be worked out at the March 11 tri-board meeting before going to the Select Board for a warrant.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records cover the same meeting and agree closely wherever a hard number appears in both (grant totals, the FY27 school budget top-line, the health-insurance rate, the March 11 Tri-Board date), but ours captures a long tail of dollar figures, side-decisions and presenters — IT capital/software line items, the override/levy figures, several staffing-cost breakdowns — that the official minutes never mention at all, and several figures where the captions clearly mis-heard a digit. The one thing a reader should know: several "decisions" in our minutes (the single school budget line, the Microsoft breakdown commitment, the EPIMS staffing data commitment) have no counterpart anywhere in the official minutes, and the $996,123 restored-positions total does not reconcile with the sum of the official's own itemized staffing requests.
